poster_title: One SPACE to Rule Them All: Jointly Mitigating Factuality and Faithfulness Hallucinations in LLMs
authors: Pengbo Wang, Chaozhuo Li, Chenxu Wang, Liwen Zheng, Litian Zhang, Xi Zhang
paper_info: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025), arXiv:2506.11088v2 [cs.CL] 23 Nov 2025

content: LLMs' practical deployment hindered by factuality and faithfulness hallucinations.
Existing methods address these issues independently, leading to performance trade-offs.
Factuality hallucinations involve contradictions against verifiable facts.
Faithfulness hallucinations involve deviations from user intent or internal inconsistencies.
Interventions targeting one type of hallucination often exacerbate the other.
SPACE (Spatial Processing for Activated Combined Embeddings) edits shared activation subspaces to mitigate both hallucinations.
Experiments conducted on TruthfulQA for factuality and PDTB for faithfulness.
Comparative baselines: TruthX and CAD models.
panels.figure_caption: Activation Distributions of Factual and Faithful Tasks

content: SPACE significantly reduced both factuality and faithfulness hallucinations compared to baselines.
panels.figure_caption: Case study on the average probe accuracies on the PDTB and TruthfulQA

content: SPACE effectively mitigates factuality and faithfulness hallucinations by targeting shared activation subspaces.
Promising direction for improving LLM reliability and trustworthiness.
